method: One tmpfiles.d directive is composed as seven space-separated fields - type, path, mode, user, group, age and argument - with a dash for an unset field and the argument written only for L. Seven types are offered: d creates a directory, e adjusts an existing directory, f creates or truncates a file, q creates a directory with a project quota, r removes a path or glob when cleaning, x excludes matching paths from cleanup and L creates a symlink. Creation types (d, e, f, q, L) produce a systemd-tmpfiles --create command and cleanup types (d, e, q, r, x) produce a --clean command, so d, e and q get both. Field applicability is enforced rather than ignored: MODE is accepted only for d, e, f and q; USER and GROUP for every type except r and x; AGE only for d, e, q, r and x; and the argument only for L, where it is required. The path must be absolute, below /, free of whitespace, quotes, backslashes, //, . and .. segments and a trailing slash, at most 4096 characters, and a glob is accepted only for r and x. MODE takes three or four octal digits, is padded to four, and is capped at 1777 so only the sticky bit can be set above 0777. A user or group is a name that starts with a letter or underscore followed by letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, or a numeric id up to 4294967294; numeric ids are rewritten without leading zeros. AGE is a systemd time span: a bare number of seconds, zero, or one or more number-unit pairs using us, ms, s, min, m, h, d, w, M and y, where M is a 30.4375-day month and y a 365.25-day year. The page reports the span in days, hours, minutes, seconds or milliseconds, so 1M reads as 30.44 days and 1h30min as 1.5 hours. The directive length, field count, file name and /etc/tmpfiles.d path are derived from the entry; the file name comes from the last path segment, drops glob characters, keeps ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, is lowercased and capped at 40 characters. Warnings cover a mode left at the created-directory default of 0755 or the file default of 0644, both owner fields left at root, a removal or exclusion with no age, an age-cleaned path outside /tmp, /var/tmp and /run, and a relative symlink target. The page composes text only: it does not read or modify the filesystem and makes no network requests.

sources.title: tmpfiles.d(5): the seven fields are type, path, mode, user, group, age and argument; d, e, f, q, r, x and L are documented types, and files in /etc/tmpfiles.d override same-named files in /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d.
systemd-tmpfiles(8): --create creates and adjusts entries while --clean removes files older than an entry's age.
systemd.time(7): time spans combine number and unit pairs such as 30d, 12h and 1h30min.
